audits.title: Evaluating Standards-Based Audit for Quality Improvement in Maternal and Newborn Care: Evidence from a multi-country implementation study
audits.standard: Facility-selected standards for maternal and newborn care, with local improvement targets
audits.setting: 128 health facilities followed up after training of 895 health workers from 211 facilities
audits.intervention: Quality improvement training in standards-based audit (traditional and blended learning), appointment of a QI champion and facility-specific targeted interventions

cycle2.result: Average follow-up score 77.4% (mean improvement 38.2%); 54% of facilities met or exceeded their improvement targets

audits.other_findings: Challenges included unrealistic target setting, resource constraints, staff shortages and supply disruptions.
audits.citation: Dickinson FM, Mwanzia L, Mohammed H, Katalambula L, Mahmoud SA, Nyaoke I, et al.. Evaluating Standards-Based Audit for Quality Improvement in Maternal and Newborn Care: Evidence from a multi-country implementation study. . 2025. doi:10.1101/2025.11.20.25340669.

audits.title: Holding up a mirror: changing obstetric practice through criterion-based clinical audit in developing countries.
audits.standard: 31 criterion-based audit criteria for good quality care of haemorrhage, eclampsia, genital tract infection, obstructed labour and uterine rupture
audits.setting: Four district hospitals in Ghana and Jamaica

cycle1.result: Many common areas for improvement identified across the four hospitals.

audits.intervention: Feedback of findings and target setting; clinical protocols, reviews of staffing and training workshops.

cycle2.result: Some aspects of clinical monitoring, drug use and record keeping improved significantly.

audits.other_findings: Criterion-based audit judged feasible and acceptable in developing country district hospitals.
audits.citation: Wagaarachchi PT, Graham WJ, Penney GC, McCaw-Binns A, Yeboah Antwi K, Hall MH. Holding up a mirror: changing obstetric practice through criterion-based clinical audit in developing countries. Int J Gynaecol Obstet. 2001;74(2):119-30; discussion 131. doi:10.1016/s0020-7292(01)00427-1. PMID: 11502289.

audits.title: Availability, distribution and use of emergency obstetric care in northern Tanzania.
audits.standard: UNICEF/UNFPA/WHO guidelines for emergency obstetric care (minimum 15% of expected deliveries in EmOC facilities)
audits.setting: All 129 delivery facilities in six districts, northern Tanzania

cycle1.result: Basic EmOC units 1.6 per 500,000 and comprehensive units 4.6 per 500,000; 36% of expected deliveries in EmOC facilities.

audits.other_findings: Large urban/rural variation; 86% of voluntary agency deliveries in qualified EmOC facilities.
audits.citation: Olsen ØE, Ndeki S, Norheim OF. Availability, distribution and use of emergency obstetric care in northern Tanzania. Health Policy Plan. 2005;20(3):167-175. doi:10.1093/heapol/czi022. PMID: 15840632.

audits.title: Effect of audit and feedback on the availability, utilisation and quality of emergency obstetric care in three districts in Malawi.
audits.standard: Criterion-based clinical audit of emergency obstetric care
audits.setting: 73 health facilities (13 hospitals and 60 health centres) in three districts in Malawi

cycle1.result: Baseline emergency obstetric care availability, utilisation and quality (details not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Facility-based maternal death reviews and criterion-based clinical audit with feedback introduced in 2006.

cycle2.result: Number of comprehensive and basic EmOC facilities did not change over 3 years (p for trend=1.000); institutional delivery rate increased overall over 3 years.

audits.other_findings: 2006 data included 43,729 women, when the institutional delivery rate dipped; the abstract is truncated for further results.
audits.citation: Kongnyuy EJ, Leigh B, van den Broek N. Effect of audit and feedback on the availability, utilisation and quality of emergency obstetric care in three districts in Malawi. Women Birth. 2008;21(4):149-155. doi:10.1016/j.wombi.2008.08.002. PMID: 18842471.

audits.title: Promoting accountability in obstetric care: use of criteria-based audit in Viet Nam.
audits.standard: National guidelines for major obstetric complications (2002) via criteria-based audit
audits.setting: Five hospitals in Thanh Hoa and Quang Tri provinces

cycle1.result: Clinical protocols for major obstetric complications were not followed; obstacles to timely treatment out of hours.

audits.intervention: Teams devised action plans to correct identified problems.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements when audit cycle repeated (no figures given).

audits.citation: Bailey PE, Binh HT, Bang HT. Promoting accountability in obstetric care: use of criteria-based audit in Viet Nam. Glob Public Health. 2010;5(1):62-74. doi:10.1080/17441690802190776. PMID: 19326280.

audits.title: Evaluation of criteria-based clinical audit in improving quality of obstetric care in a developing country hospital.
audits.standard: Standard criteria for management of obstetric haemorrhage, eclampsia, genital tract infection, obstructed labour and uterine rupture

cycle1.result: Overall care: obstetric haemorrhage 61%, eclampsia 54.3%, obstructed labour 81.7%, genital tract sepsis 66%.

audits.intervention: Mechanisms for improving care identified and implemented after Phase I.

cycle2.result: Obstetric haemorrhage 81% (p = 0.000), eclampsia 90% (p = 0.00), obstructed labour 93.5% (p < 0.001), genital tract sepsis 85.2% (p < 0.01).

audits.other_findings: 65 patients audited across both phases; clinical monitoring, drug use and urgent senior attention also improved.
audits.citation: Hunyinbo KI, Fawole AO, Sotiloye OS, Otolorin EO. Evaluation of criteria-based clinical audit in improving quality of obstetric care in a developing country hospital. Afr J Reprod Health. 2008;12(3):59-70. PMID: 19435013.

audits.title: Use of a criteria-based audit to optimize uptake of cesarean delivery in a low-resource setting.
audits.standard: Criteria-based audit checklist for obstructed labour and fetal distress
audits.setting: Muhimbili National Hospital, Dar es Salaam (tertiary referral hospital)

cycle1.result: Perinatal morbidity and mortality with obstructed labour 42/260 (16.2%); fetal distress baseline n=248.

cycle2.result: Perinatal morbidity and mortality with obstructed labour 22/250 (8.8%) (P=0.012); fetal distress re-audit n=251.

audits.other_findings: Using Robson classification in 27,960 parturients, caesarean rate for preterm pregnancies increased (referred OR 1.28; non-referred OR 2.78) and neonatal distress decreased in several groups.
audits.citation: Mgaya AH, Kidanto HL, Nyström L, Essén B. Use of a criteria-based audit to optimize uptake of cesarean delivery in a low-resource setting. Int J Gynaecol Obstet. 2019;144(2):199-209. doi:10.1002/ijgo.12726. PMID: 30499099.

audits.title: Standards-based audit to improve quality of maternal and newborn care-A stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial in Malawi.
audits.standard: 25 locally agreed standards of emergency obstetric and newborn care
audits.setting: 44 healthcare facilities (health centres and hospitals) in Malawi

cycle1.result: Crude overall compliance 45% in control phase (51.6% at basic and 34.5% at comprehensive EmONC facilities).

audits.intervention: Local review of findings and changes such as staff re-orientation, staff meetings, improved supervision and ensuring equipment and consumables (thermometers, rapid tests, partographs) were available.

cycle2.result: Crude overall compliance 63% (70.6% basic, 50.8% comprehensive); adjusted OR 2.80 (95% CI 1.65-4.76).

audits.other_findings: Stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial of standards-based audit; 25 women assessed per compliance measurement.
audits.citation: White SA, Mgawadere F, Gopalakrishnan S, van den Broek N. Standards-based audit to improve quality of maternal and newborn care-A stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial in Malawi. PLoS One. 2024;19(9):e0310896. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0310896. PMID: 39348372.

audits.title: Criteria based clinical audit of selected obstetric emergencies standard of care and feto-maternal outcomes in public hospitals of West Shoa Zone, Central Ethiopia.
audits.standard: Criteria-based standards of care for selected obstetric emergencies
audits.setting: Public hospitals of West Shoa Zone

cycle1.result: Care met standards in 83.2% for severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, 82% for antepartum haemorrhage, 82.8% for obstructed labour and 78.4% for postpartum haemorrhage

audits.other_findings: Maternal mortality 684.9/100,000 live births and perinatal mortality 114.2/1000.
audits.citation: Damme TG, Demissie DB, Abeya SG. Criteria based clinical audit of selected obstetric emergencies standard of care and feto-maternal outcomes in public hospitals of West Shoa Zone, Central Ethiopia. BMC Pregnancy Childbirth. 2026;26(1):1034. doi:10.1186/s12884-026-09563-7. PMID: 42387429.
